concerns.text: Gradual 12-pound central weight gain over 4 months on morning-and-evening maintenance hydrocortisone is clearly non-emergent, though clinicians may reasonably route replacement glucocorticoid dose adjustment either to a primary-care physician visit (level 2) or directly to the patient's outpatient endocrinology clinic (level 3).

A slower urinary stream without retention after 4 nights of oral decongestant pills in a 76-year-old man fits a routine primary-care evaluation for underlying prostatic obstruction and medication review (level 2), though some clinicians would first advise stopping the decongestant at home and observing whether stream strength normalizes (level 1).

Unassessed 7 kg weight loss over 3 months despite big meals with bilateral hand trembling and a resting pulse of 108 beats a minute in a 29 year old woman is labelled specialist (level 3) for endocrinology evaluation of suspected thyrotoxicosis, though whether initial thyroid blood tests and beta-blocker initiation start with a general physician (level 2) before specialist referral is a clinician's call.

Having the last monthly period start 7 months ago after previously regular 28-day cycles in a 25 year old woman is labelled specialist (level 3) for gynecology or reproductive endocrinology evaluation of secondary amenorrhea, though whether initial pregnancy exclusion and baseline hormone testing begin with a general physician or clinic (level 2) before specialist care is a clinician's call.

Six weeks of recurrent retrosternal solid-meat dysphagia in a 63-year-old adult requires upper gastrointestinal endoscopy, so depending on healthcare system access a clinician could route initial presentation either to an urgent primary-care physician visit for fast-track referral (level 2) or directly to an outpatient gastroenterology specialist (level 3).

Acute weeping vesicular allergic contact dermatitis under a watch clasp typically benefits from prescription-potency topical corticosteroid therapy at an outpatient clinic (level 2), though once the metal watch is removed some clinicians would trial pharmacist-guided over-the-counter topical hydrocortisone and cool compresses first (level 1).

Heavy sweating and a brief transient dizzy spell after 4 hours on a hot factory floor with an afebrile 97 F oral temperature is appropriate for cool-room rest and oral fluid hydration (level 1), though an occupational or primary-care clinician might reasonably advise a non-urgent clinic check before returning to floor work (level 2).
